method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading; exact macro, identifier, token and formula comparison; and a model-theoretic replay of the standard/non-standard distinction and the incompleteness example. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The models-of-arithmetic introduction: the standard natural-number structure, an isomorphic string-domain presentation, compactness-based non-standard models, standard numerals and the consistency-statement example.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The standard arithmetic structure has domain N and the usual zero, successor, addition and multiplication operations. Replacing each natural number by a finite string of a's yields a structure with the same relationships, hence an isomorphic structure.
samples.checks: All four interpretation equations, the two domains and the distinction between changing domain elements and preserving their interpreted relationships are intact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Compactness gives models of every theory true in N that are not isomorphic to N. In a standard model every element is the value of a standard numeral; a non-standard model has at least one element unequal to every such value.
samples.checks: The universal quantification over all n, the existential non-standard element and the isomorphism criterion retain their original scopes.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Non-standard elements behave as infinite natural numbers and explain how PA plus the negation of its consistency statement can have models. Such a model contains a non-standard witness coded as a PA derivation of contradiction, although PA refutes every standard numeral as that witness.
samples.checks: The consistency sentence, both independence claims, non-satisfaction by N, model conclusion and final standard-numeral refutations are preserved. The malformed one-argument proof-predicate occurrence is repaired to use the bound witness x as its first argument.

source_observations: MR-P126 directly attests संख्यांक for numeral and MR-P127 directly attests उत्तरवर्ती for successor; the full model-theory compounds remain source-defined and reviewable.
मानक and प्रतिमान follow existing edition decisions; OpenLogic itself controls the standard/non-standard contrast by isomorphism and exhaustion by numeral values.

The frozen source's existential witness formula omits x from the binary proof predicate even though the consistency definition and final numeral instances both supply that first argument; OLFOL-029 records the bounded correction.
All macros, identifiers, controlled tokens and unaffected formulas match the frozen source; the one corrected formula passes the documented source-correction projection.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
No exact authoritative Marathi headwords were found for the complete compounds standard model, non-standard model, standard numeral, incompleteness phenomenon or Gödel number.
